sample_unit: patients (research EHR cases and controls; 34 rare disease algorithms)

links.outcome: Negative likelihood ratio and sensitivity of rare disease case-finding algorithms
links.effect: Median sensitivity 3.8% (IQR 1.2–12.6%); median negative likelihood ratio 0.96 (IQR 0.87–0.99), so a negative result adds little information.
links.quote: Median positive likelihood ratio was 1167 (IQR: 125–4006), reflecting a strong signal for disease presence, and median negative likelihood ratio was 0.96 (IQR: 0.87–0.99), reflecting limited clinical utility of a negative result.

screen.reason: Retrospective validation study of MendelScan, an AI-based rare disease case-finding tool evaluating performance metrics and feasibility for deployment.
